root_cause.text: The bit-field masks for the GENERIC_CMD register in the IPA v5.0+ GSI register definitions were incorrectly specified (wrong bit positions and widths) compared to the actual hardware layout, causing the driver to program the register incorrectly and trigger a kernel warning when issuing a stop command to the MPSS remoteproc.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes the GENERIC_CHID mask from GENMASK(9,5) to GENMASK(12,5), GENERIC_EE from GENMASK(13,10) to GENMASK(16,13), and adds a new GENERIC_PARAMS field (GENMASK(31,24)). The commit message explicitly states: "Fix the field masks to match the hardware layout documented in downstream GSI" and "Notably this fixes a WARN I was seeing when I tried to send 'stop' to the MPSS remoteproc while IPA was up." (Ref: patch diff replacing the register field masks in `drivers/net/ipa/reg/gsi_reg-v5.0.c`.)

intent_record.intent_summary: Update GENERIC_CMD field masks to match revised hardware register definition, expanding CHID, shifting EE, and adding a PARAMS field.
intent_record.what: Changed bit masks for GENERIC_CHID from GENMASK(9,5) to GENMASK(12,5) and GENERIC_EE from GENMASK(13,10) to GENMASK(16,13), updated reserved bits comment from 'Bits 14-31' to 'Bits 17-23', and added a new entry GENERIC_PARAMS with GENMASK(31,24).
intent_record.how: The register layout for GENERIC_CMD is redefined: CHID now occupies bits 5-12 (8 bits instead of 5), EE occupies bits 13-16 (shifted from bits 10-13), a new PARAMS field occupies bits 24-31, and reserved bits are reduced to bits 17-23. Runtime behavior changes because code using these masks will read/write different bit positions and widths.
